Day 4, 09:15 Local Time, 07:15 GMT, 12:45 IST: Hello and welcome to another sunny morning in Gqeberha. After the gloom of the first couple of days, the weather has cleared up and South Africa's fortunes in this Test have somewhat mimicked the same. From a position where the series seemed to be slipping away, they're now the only team with a realistic chance of pushing for a win - all thanks to captain Temba Bavuma and his incredible knock of 179, and also the efforts of Marco Jansen and Simon Harmer. The most obvious route towards a win would be to bowl Australia out cheaply and enforce the follow-on. The pitch, as Bavuma described it, is one where the batter is never in. There's a bit of nibble, and South Africa have four seamers who can exploit it, led by KG Rabada who marked his return from injury last evening with a wicket in his first over. Should be fun to see him unleashed this morning.

Harmer 2/2: [You smashed Boland for six to reach 49] I think the whole time I was looking to put the bowlers under pressure on the short ball. But a lot of the times it's coming at like your left ear and you just end up getting out the way. Bit of a top edge on that one, but when I saw it, once I'd hit it and looked up and found the ball, I was like, okay, that should be six. So, yeah, I've been in the 30s and 40s a few times. So to be one away from 50, I was like, okay, we're in a better place here. [Your first Test fifty, after two first-class hundreds. How did it feel?] I think it sort of was on and around third fork stump and then came onto my hip. And I remember clipping it down to fine leg and just saying to myself, yes, man! Nice to finally get to that 50 mark. Yeah, and to score some runs when it matters.

Bavuma's thoughts on the pitch today: The biggest thing with St George's on Day 4 and 5 are the divots. The divots aren't as pronounced as usual. Hasn't broken as much, so spin might not be as much of a factor.

Pitch report | Shaun Pollock: Hasn't changed much (the pitch). It's definitely a new ball surface. These first 5-10 overs are key. There are little divots that you can work with, but not as many as you get on a Day 4 surface.
